label: single-host court; conformance shim for the 3FS USRBIO ABI, not a 3FS run; synthetic fixtures; local filesystem
losses: The scalar side reuses its destinations while the ring side returns owned vectors and allocates per rep; the ring number is therefore an upper bound on its cost, not a like-for-like win.
The USRBIO path opens and registers one descriptor per read. A production adapter should keep immutable keys registered; this receipt prices the cost of not doing so.
The shim performs pread per request inside wait_for_ios, so the batched path cannot exhibit a transport advantage; any difference it shows is adapter overhead, not 3FS behaviour.
No 3FS deployment, no RDMA, no kernel bypass, no multi-node consistency test.
The store's write phase enters through the ring for staging only; fsync and rename still order each publication, so this is not a write-throughput claim.

transport.note: hf3fs_is_hf3fs=false: this library is the conformance shim, so no 3FS throughput, latency, RDMA, or deployment claim follows from this receipt
